description: In less than two centuries, the Aztecs built a capital of 200,000 people on a lake. Their empire, founded on tribute and sacrifice, collapsed in two years once the Spanish arrived.

hero.hook: A city built on water, bigger than London. Then, in two years, nothing.

blocks.text: In the heart of what is now Mexico, the Aztecs built a capital on a lake in less than two centuries, home to **200,000 people**. Bigger than London or Rome at the time. Their power mixed hydraulic engineering, a demanding religion, and permanent war.
Between **1519** and **1521**, that empire fell apart. Not only under the guns of Cortés, the Spanish conquistador, but under the hatred of its own subjects and under an invisible weapon: disease.

The **Mexica**, the people later called the Aztecs, came from the mythical [[Aztlán]], a homeland somewhere to the north. They reached the Valley of Mexico in the 13th century. Despised by their neighbors, they looked for a sign from their god [[Huitzilopochtli]], god of the sun and of war: an eagle devouring a snake on a cactus. In **1325** they found it on an islet in Lake **Texcoco**. So [[Tenochtitlán]], their future capital, was born.
To feed the city, they perfected the [[chinampas]], ultra-fertile artificial islands made of mud and plants. Three causeways, dikes, canals: the city became a lake fortress and a giant marketplace.
The Aztecs did not use the wheel for transport and had no pack animals. They still moved millions of tons of stone for their pyramids.

sections.title: From marshland to a capital on the water

blocks.text: In **1428**, Tenochtitlán joined with two neighboring cities, Texcoco and Tlacopan: the **Triple Alliance**. Soon the Mexica ruled alone. Their empire did not absorb the peoples it beat. It demanded regular **tribute**: corn, cacao, feathers, metals. The wealth of the capital fed the hatred of its subject peoples, such as the [[Tlaxcaltecs]], fierce enemies of the Aztecs.

blocks.caption: Tenochtitlán, the lake metropolis at the heart of the Aztec empire

blocks.text: It was a war machine that needed constant conquest. When the Spanish arrived, all they had to do was gather up those resentments.
Cacao beans served as money. In Tenochtitlán a rabbit cost ten beans, and a slave in good health about a hundred.

According to the [[Five Suns Cosmogony]], an Aztec myth, the sun survives only if it is fed with human blood. At the [[Templo Mayor]], the great pyramid at the center of the city, sacrifice was not gratuitous cruelty. For the Aztecs it was what kept the world turning.

In **1519**, **Hernán Cortés** landed with a few hundred Spaniards. [[Moctezuma II]], the Aztec emperor, hesitated. Steel, firearms, and horses frightened his people. But the main killer was [[smallpox]], a European disease against which local populations had no immunity. Cortés laid siege to the capital with thousands of indigenous allies.

events.title: Fall of Tenochtitlán

blocks.text: In **1521**, after **80 days** of siege, Tenochtitlán fell. Starved, cut off from fresh water, ravaged by disease. Its stones were used to build Mexico City, the capital of [[New Spain]], the Spanish colony.

Not everything vanished. The [[chinampas]] are still there. [[Nahuatl]], the language of the Aztecs, is spoken by more than a million people. The eagle and the snake remain the emblem of Mexico. A brilliant civilization survives in memory and in the landscape.
The Aztecs built a city of **200,000** people on a lake. Their tribute system and [[smallpox]] let a few hundred Spaniards, helped by local allies, destroy the empire in two years.
